A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SLMRec study and provide readable text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. The title change and relocated related work do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original recommendation experiments on four Amazon18 domains, including accuracy, efficiency, layer-depth studies, knowledge-distillation experiments, and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds self-supervised baseline results and an inference-time comparison with SASRec and MAERec.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the same architecture, blockwise feature distillation, cosine and norm losses, multiple supervision, and training objective. Figure 3 clarifies the existing supervision paths without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate sequential recommendation on the same Amazon18 Cloth, Movie, Music, and Sport domains. No additional dataset, task, or distinct input scenario is reported.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 add a self-supervised comparator category comprising S3-Rec, DuoRec, and MAERec across all four datasets. Appendix B.4 also adds SASRec and MAERec to the inference-efficiency comparisons, substantially broadening the evaluated alternatives.

E3.justification: Tables 2–3 introduce average-rank summaries, and new Table 8 reports relative performance improvement alongside inference time under a shared A100 GPU and batch-size-512 setting. Existing splits, negative sampling, training settings, and recommendation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The layer-depth experiments, online-distillation and block-number studies, and loss-component ablations are retained. In particular, v2 Table 8 becomes v3 Table 9 with identical results. Added baseline accuracy and timing comparisons do not introduce an ablation, robustness test, or error analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies experimental seed or repeated-run counts or reports confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new average-rank summaries do not add uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds comparative results for three self-supervised methods across all four datasets and new average ranks, including 1.50 and 1.25 for SLMRec in Tables 2–3. New Table 8 reports inference times of 0.015, 0.061, and 0.052 hours for SASRec, MAERec, and SLMRec, respectively. Retained accuracy scores, original efficiency results, and ablation values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 6 retains the same attention-propagation formulation and two propositions. Appendix A preserves their proofs and derivations, including Equations 10–26; no substantive mathematical revision is present.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims about layer redundancy, distilling competitive small recommenders, approximately 13% of parameters, and 6.6x/8.0x training/inference speedups. Online distillation and theoretical justification were already claimed in v2.

C2.justification: Appendix B.4 newly interprets the traditional-model timing comparison as supporting practical deployment with comparable computational efficiency and nearly 50% performance improvement over SASRec. The existing limitations concerning few-shot adaptation and retraining remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B.3 adds implementation provenance and code links for the new self-supervised baselines. SLMRec's hyperparameter table, mixed-precision and GPU information, and code/data access statements are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references and descriptions for S3-Rec, DuoRec, and MAERec, plus Jin et al. (2025) on knowledge across model layers. The central novelty positioning remains stable; most of Appendix C reproduces related work already present in v2 Section 7.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, publication headers are updated, and three related-work topics move into Appendix C, fixing the previous unresolved appendix reference. Baseline descriptions expand locally, while most methodological and explanatory prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 2–3 gain baseline rows, rank columns, and revised highlighting; a new efficiency table is added. Figure 3 redraws the supervision adapters and scoring paths, Table 1 is wrapped beside text, and existing figures and tables are resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: The added self-supervised baselines and traditional-model timing comparison strengthen the empirical context, while implementation links and the clearer Figure 3 improve usability. The gain is limited: the underlying method and retained findings are unchanged, and the new claim of comparable efficiency needs qualification because Table 8 reports SLMRec taking 0.052 hours versus SASRec's 0.015 hours.
